correctness.rationale: For each functional, the explicit associative path products yield all stabilizer equations from primitive idempotents and arrow/path spaces. Nonzero path-pairing rank s gives precisely two solvability regimes. In the interior regime the two scalar equations agree by evaluating the same pairing twice; when they fail the remaining radical equation is genuinely independent. Unit stabilizer orders \((q-1)^2q^{a+b+ab-2s-1}\) and \((q-1)q^{a+b+ab-2s-2}\) give the last two orbit sizes, with separate direct handling at C=0. Gaussian matrix-rank counts and division by orbit size give all five rows. Every functional belongs to exactly one row; weighted totals equal \(q^{3+a+b+ab}\). Direct finite-field stabilizer checks, including characteristic two and the order-four extension field, and 288 independent mass specializations pass. General validity comes from proof, not tests.

value.rationale: The path algebra with two successive nonzero arrow spaces is a minimal natural hereditary algebra with nonzero radical-square multiplication, in contrast to radical-square-zero quiver algebras. Its coadjoint orbit-size spectrum for the full unit group is a natural finite representation-theoretic invariant. The theorem gives all sizes and multiplicities for arbitrary arrow multiplicities and finite fields, and quantitatively distinguishes the rank of the length-two composition pairing and whether arrow functionals lie in its two image spaces. The classification is neither a single sample nor a mere normalization check.
